content.title: About
content.content: Black bean salad is a dish made from cooked black beans, fresh vegetables (tomatoes, onion, bell pepper), herbs, and a dressing based on olive oil, lime or vinegar. It offers a rich aroma, a mildly tangy‑sweet flavor, and a pleasant texture thanks to crunchy veggies and soft beans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans, also called turtle beans, originate from South America and have been cultivated for over 7,000 years.
The dark color comes from anthocyanin antioxidants that are abundant in the beans.
Traditional Mexican versions often add corn, avocado, and cilantro.
The salad is easily adapted to a vegan diet, requiring no dairy ingredients.
It keeps its flavor well in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Black beans provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, making them a valuable protein source for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals aid energy metabolism, muscle function, and healthy blood.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The salad raises blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking beans before cooking helps mitigate this.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Beans can cause bloating in sensitive people; gradual introduction to the diet lessens the effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish, a side for meat or fish, or as a filling for tacos and burritos. It can be stored in the fridge and dressed just before serving to keep the vegetables crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep the dressing separate so the vegetables stay crunchy.
